extracted.intended_audience: public housing authorities (PHAs), housing owners, responsible entities, HUD administrators, and practitioners who determine eligibility and rents under HUD-assisted housing programs
extracted.subtask_short: HUD income and adjusted income rules
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and standards for defining, calculating, and adjusting family annual income and adjusted income for HUD-assisted housing (public housing, Section 8/HCV, moderate rehabilitation), including exclusions, deductions, hardship relief, verification, and PHA/welfare-agency coordination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual income — inclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual income includes all amounts, not specifically excluded, received from all sources by each family member 18 or older or who is head/spouse, plus unearned income for dependents under 18; when net family assets exceed $50,000, imputed returns on the asset based on the current passbook savings rate may be included if actual returns cannot be calculated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to determine eligibility and rent for initial occupancy, interim reexaminations, and annual reexaminations. HUD adjusts the $50,000 threshold annually by CPI for urban wage earners and clerical workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual income — exclusions (enumerated list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific categories of receipts that are not included in annual income for HUD purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Exclusions include (but are not limited to): imputed return on assets when net family assets ≤ $50,000; certain trust distributions (irreversible or revocable outside family control) and income used for minor's medical care; earned income of children under 18; foster care/kinship/guardianship payments; insurance payments and settlements for personal/property losses; reimbursements for health/medical care; amounts recovered in malpractice/negligence suits leading to disability; income of live-in aide, foster child/adult; assistance excluded under HEA §479B; student financial assistance expressly for tuition/books/room/board and housing costs (with detailed subrules on when such assistance is excluded and verification requirements); income/distributions from Coverdell/529/baby-bond accounts; special pay for family members exposed to hostile fire; PASS amounts set aside; program reimbursements for out-of-pocket expenses to participate in programs; resident service stipends (≤ $200/month); incremental earnings from HUD-funded or qualifying training programs (only while participating); reparation payments from foreign governments for Nazi persecution; certain earned income of dependent students and adoption assistance payments beyond certain deductions; deferred periodic SSI/SS/VA benefits received as lump sums or prospective monthly amounts; aid-and-attendance payments to veterans; property tax refund/rebate payments; Medicaid or other agency payments enabling a disabled family member to reside in assisted unit; loan proceeds (net disbursed); tribal mismanagement claim payments excluded from gross income; amounts HUD is statutorily required to exclude; replacement housing 'gap' payments under 49 CFR part 24 (subject to conditions); nonrecurring income (with examples such as limited census employment, stimulus payments, state refundable tax credits/refunds, gifts, in-kind donations, lump-sum asset additions); civil rights settlements/judgments; retirement plan account income (except distributions when received); income earned on Family Self-Sufficiency Account amounts; self-employment income rules specifying net income, depreciation, and withdrawals policies, etc.

For student financial assistance: detailed subcriteria define what counts as excluded student aid, what does not, requirements that aid be expressly for covered costs, methods for calculating the excluded portion when combined with other excluded assistance, and verification requirements by the responsible entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of family income — procedures and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for estimating or determining family income depending on the action: initial occupancy, interim reexamination, or annual reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1) For initial occupancy or initial provision of assistance and for interim reexaminations, the PHA/owner must estimate income for the upcoming 12-month period. 2) For annual reexaminations, the PHA/owner must determine income for the previous 12-month period and use that amount, except where streamlined income determination rules apply. 3) When previous 12-month determinations were adjusted due to interim reexaminations, the PHA/owner must consider those redeterminations and make adjustments to reflect current income if income changed during the period and was not accounted for. 4) Use of other programs' income determinations is permitted under specified verification methods (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of other programs' income determinations and verification
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs/owners may rely on annual income determinations made within the previous 12 months for certain means-tested Federal public assistance programs, subject to verification requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed programs include TANF, Medicaid, SNAP, EITC, Low-Income Housing Credit, WIC, SSI, and others HUD designates. If using another program's determination, the PHA/owner must obtain appropriate third-party verification indicating family size/composition and annual income, and must follow HUD requirements on how recently the verification may be considered current. If third-party verification is unavailable or family disputes the other program's determination, the PHA/owner must calculate annual income under 24 CFR part 5, subpart F.

rubrics_metrics.name: De minimis errors in income calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Small calculation errors in family income determinations do not automatically constitute noncompliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A de minimis error is where the PHA/owner determination deviates from the correct income by no more than $30 per month in monthly adjusted income ($360 in annual adjusted income). PHAs/owners must still take corrective action to credit or repay families overcharged; families are not required to repay for undercharges due to de minimis errors. HUD may revise the de minimis amount by rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusted income — mandatory deductions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adjusted income is annual income after mandatory deductions defined by HUD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mandatory deductions include: $480 for each dependent (HUD-adjusted annually and rounded down to next $25), $525 for any elderly or disabled family (HUD-adjusted annually and rounded down to next $25), the sum of unreimbursed health and medical care expenses of elderly/disabled family members and attendant care/auxiliary apparatus expenses for disabled members to enable employment to the extent that sum exceeds 10% of annual income (with the attendant care deduction limited to the combined earned income of family members 18+ who can work because of such care), and any reasonable child care expenses necessary to enable employment or further education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjusted income — additional deductions and PHA/owner options
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs/owners may adopt additional deductions beyond HUD mandatory deductions, subject to program-specific constraints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For public housing, HCV, and Section 8 moderate rehabilitation programs, a PHA that adopts additional deductions must establish a written policy; public housing PHAs that adopt deductions forgo eligibility for certain increases in Capital Fund and Operating Fund formula grants related to those deductions. For HCV and moderate rehabilitation, PHAs must have funding to cover increased assistance costs; deductions must be included in the HCV administrative plan or a written policy for moderate rehabilitation. Responsible entities administering HUD programs listed in §5.601(d) must calculate permitted additional deductions as required by applicable program regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial hardship relief — phased-in relief for statutory threshold change
rubrics_metrics.description: Phased-in relief is provided for families affected by the statutory increase in the threshold for the health/medical/attendant care deduction from annual income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requires that the family received a deduction as of Jan 1, 2024, because their eligible expenses exceeded 3% of annual income. Relief phases in as follows: initially the family receives a deduction for the portion of eligible expenses exceeding 5% of annual income; 12 months later the threshold becomes expenses exceeding 7.5%; 24 months later the threshold becomes expenses exceeding 10% (after which only the general hardship option may remain). A family may request to switch earlier to the general hardship rule; if approved, their relief is administered under the general hardship provision and they can no longer receive phased-in relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial hardship relief — general hardship exemption for elderly/disabled or families with changed circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate hardship relief is available for elderly/disabled families or families experiencing a financial hardship due to changed circumstances that would not otherwise trigger an interim reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requires demonstrating increased eligible expenses or a qualifying change in circumstances (as defined by the responsible entity). Relief provides a deduction for the sum of eligible expenses exceeding 5% of annual income. Relief ends when qualifying circumstances no longer apply or after 90 days, whichever is earlier; responsible entities may extend for additional 90-day periods at their discretion while hardship continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemption to continue child care expense deduction
rubrics_metrics.description: A family losing eligibility for the child care deduction may request a hardship exemption to continue the deduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To qualify, the family must demonstrate to the responsible entity's satisfaction that they are unable to pay rent because of loss of the deduction and that the child care expense is still necessary even though the family member is no longer employed or furthering education. If approved, the exemption and alternative adjusted income calculation remain in place for up to 90 days, with possible discretionary extensions in 90-day increments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hardship policy requirements for responsible entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Responsible entities must define hardship policies and inform families about hardship-related adjustments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entity must establish how it defines hardship (including inability to pay rent) for purposes of hardship exemptions, and must promptly notify the family in writing of any change in adjusted income and rent resulting from the hardship exemption, including when the exemption begins and expires (i.e., per phased-in or 90-day timelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on assistance to students enrolled in higher education (§5.612)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility exclusion: No Section 8 assistance shall be provided to an individual who simultaneously meets all specified student-related criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual is ineligible for Section 8 if they: (a) are enrolled as a student at an institution of higher education (per HEA §102); (b) are under 24 years of age; (c) are not a U.S. military veteran; (d) are unmarried; (e) do not have a dependent child; (f) are not a person with disabilities (as defined) and were not receiving Section 8 as of Nov 30, 2005; and (g) are not otherwise individually eligible and whose parents are not eligible on income grounds to receive Section 8. (All listed conditions must be met for denial.)

rubrics_metrics.name: PHA cooperation with welfare agencies (§5.613)
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs administering public housing and Section 8 tenant-based assistance must make best efforts to enter into cooperation agreements with welfare agencies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cooperation agreements should target public assistance, benefits, and services to families in HUD programs to achieve self-sufficiency, and should provide written verification of welfare benefits for families applying for or receiving assistance in these housing programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imputed welfare income — definition, when included, and limitations (§5.615)
rubrics_metrics.description: Imputed welfare income is the amount of annual income not actually received due to a specified welfare benefit reduction but nonetheless included in a family's annual income for rent determination when certain conditions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to 'covered families' who receive welfare benefits where law requires participation in economic self-sufficiency programs. 'Specified welfare benefit reduction' means a reduction by the welfare agency for fraud by a family member or welfare agency sanction for noncompliance with participation requirements. It does not include reductions for expiration of time limits, inability to obtain employment despite compliance, or reductions for other welfare agency requirements. The PHA includes imputed welfare income in annual income during the term of the welfare benefit reduction (as reported by the welfare agency), offsets imputed welfare income by any additional income commencing after the sanction (reducing it to zero if additional income equals or exceeds the imputed amount), and may not include imputed welfare income if the family was not an assisted resident at the time of the sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review procedures for PHA determinations of imputed welfare income
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for families to challenge PHA determinations about imputed welfare income differ by program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public housing tenants who dispute the PHA's calculation get a written denial with brief explanation and may request a grievance hearing under part 966, subpart B; they are not required to pay an escrow deposit under §966.55(e) for the imputed-welfare-income portion to obtain the grievance hearing. Section 8 participants may request an informal hearing under §982.555; PHAs must provide written notice with brief explanation and the opportunity for the hearing per applicable hearing procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: PHA relationship with welfare agency — information exchange obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: PHAs must request welfare agencies to inform them about specified welfare benefit reductions affecting families.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PHA must ask welfare agencies to inform the PHA in writing of any specified welfare benefit reduction, the reason and term of the reduction, and any subsequent determinations affecting the amount or term, so the PHA can determine imputed welfare income. The welfare agency must, at the PHA's request, inform the PHA of the amount and term of reductions and any changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility allowance — definition and use
rubrics_metrics.description: When utilities (except telephone) and other housing services are the family's responsibility, the utility allowance is the PHA/HUD-estimated monthly cost of reasonable consumption by an energy-conservative modest household.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The allowance is used to calculate tenant payments where utilities are not included in tenant rent; must be consistent with requirements of a safe, sanitary, and healthful living environment and is an estimate made or approved by the PHA or HUD.

rubrics_metrics.name: Utility reimbursement — definition and application
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility reimbursement is the amount, if any, by which the utility allowance for a unit exceeds the family's total tenant payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not used in the Section 8 voucher program or for public housing families paying a flat rent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust funds not revocable/under family control — asset exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: If a trust fund is established and is not revocable by, or under the control of, any family/household member, the trust fund is not a family asset and its value is excluded from net family assets calculation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exclusion applies so long as the fund remains in a trust not revocable by or under the control of any family/household member; relevant when determining whether to impute returns or include trust distributions as income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference to program-specific definitions of Owner/Responsible Entity
rubrics_metrics.description: The terms 'owner' and 'responsible entity' are defined in applicable program regulations and may include borrowers in certain program contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For §5.611 and related provisions, specific definitions apply: responsible entity for §5.611 includes Owner as defined in 24 CFR 891.205 for Section 202 Supportive Housing, Borrower as defined in 24 CFR 891.505 for Section 202 Direct Loans, and Owner as defined in 24 CFR 891.305 for Section 811 Supportive Housing. Practitioners must consult the relevant program regulation for exact application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Very low income family — definition
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'very low income family' is one whose annual income does not exceed 50% of the median family income for the area as determined by HUD, with HUD-authorized adjustments for family size or area-specific conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HUD may set income ceilings higher or lower than 50% where necessary because of unusually high or low family incomes in the area.
